Headline: Argentina’s 2025/26 Corn Crop Forecast Raised to Record 70.5 Million Tonnes
Summary: Argentina’s 2025/26 corn production forecast has been raised to a record 70.5 million tonnes, from the previous estimate of 68.0 million tonnes, mainly due to a larger-than-expected planted area. Around 75% of the planned area has been harvested, although progress is behind last year’s pace due to unusually wet and warm weather in July. For the 2026/27 season, corn production is initially forecast at 66.0 million tonnes, while planted area is expected to decline by 7.3% year-on-year.

Headline: Tur Imports Surge 43% on Higher African Shipments
Summary: India’s tur imports increased 43% to 5.05 lakh tonnes during January–June 2026, from 3.53 lakh tonnes in the same period last year. Mozambique was the largest supplier at 1.84 lakh tonnes, followed by Tanzania at 1.01 lakh tonnes and Sudan at 49,049 tonnes. Imports strengthened in June to 77,830 tonnes, with higher supplies from Mozambique and other origins. The sharp rise in imports is expected to improve domestic availability and limit near-term upside in tur prices.

Headline: Urad Imports Decline 19% as Myanmar Shipments Remain Dominant
Summary: India’s urad imports fell 19% to 3.40 lakh tonnes during January–June 2026, from 4.21 lakh tonnes in the same period last year. Myanmar remained the largest supplier at 2.78 lakh tonnes, followed by Brazil at 39,309 tonnes. Monthly imports declined sharply during April–May before recovering to 46,820 tonnes in June. Lower imports could provide some near-term support to domestic urad prices, although rising Kharif sowing and upcoming supplies remain key factors.

Headline: India Kharif Pulse Sowing Down 0.32% as Urad Gains Offset Lower Tur and Moong Acreage
Summary: India’s Kharif pulse sowing stood at 108.14 lakh hectares as of 14 August 2026, down 0.32% from 108.49 lakh hectares last year. Tur acreage declined 4.05% to 40.31 lakh hectares, while Moong fell 4.10% to 32.05 lakh hectares. In contrast, Urad sowing increased 13.13% to 23.52 lakh hectares, while Moth Bean and Kulthi also recorded gains. Overall acreage remains broadly near last year’s level, though lower Tur and Moong sowing remains a key supply concern.

Headline: Pakistan Considers Wheat Imports from Kazakhstan
Summary: Pakistan and Kazakhstan are working to expand agricultural trade, with wheat supply becoming a key area of cooperation. Kazakhstan has shown interest in supplying wheat to Pakistan, while Pakistan will evaluate the proposal based on price, quality and supply conditions. Better rail and transport links between Central Asia and Pakistan could reduce freight costs and support future wheat trade. If the proposal moves ahead, Kazakhstan could become an additional source of wheat for Pakistan and help strengthen domestic supply.

Headline: Thailand Sugar Cane Output May Decline on Super El Nino Risk
Summary: Thailand’s sugar cane production could decline to around 100 million tonnes in 2026-27, from 106 million tonnes last season, as the potential impact of a “Super El Nino” raises concerns over drought and irregular rainfall. Khon Kaen Sugar Industry Plc (KSL) said prolonged dry conditions could reduce both cane yields and planting area, with some farmers considering shifting to cassava due to better prices. Lower Thai cane production could tighten global sugar supplies and support prices, with KSL forecasting global sugar prices could rise to around 17 cents per pound in 2027, compared with about 16 cents currently. The company has advised Thai sugar producers to slow exports and build inventories ahead of the 2026-27 crushing season, which is scheduled from December 2026 to March 2027.

Headline: Sugar Prices Rise Amid Tight Supply Concerns
Summary: Sugar prices have risen sharply in India amid concerns over tight supplies at the end of the 2025-26 season, with the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories (NFCSF) urging the Centre to disclose sugar stock estimates from its ongoing physical verification of mills to curb speculation. End-season stocks are expected to fall to around 350 thousand tonnes, while all-India sugar prices have increased 8% in retail and 7% in wholesale markets over the past month. The government has imposed stock limits and asked mills to begin crushing early in October to boost initial-season production, but supplies could remain tight in November before improving from December. Industry officials also expect the government to consider restricting sugar diversion towards ethanol if domestic availability remains under pressure. Around 240 thousand tonnes of sugar is estimated to be diverted for ethanol during the current season, compared with 340 thousand tonnes in 2024-25.

Headline: French Maize Crop Rating Falls to 29% in Good or Excellent Condition
Summary: France’s maize crop condition has deteriorated sharply, with only 29% of the crop rated in good or excellent condition as of August 10, 2026. The decline reflects the impact of persistent heat and dry weather across major maize-growing regions, raising concerns over yield potential. France is a key maize producer in the European Union, and continued weather stress could further reduce the country’s maize output and tighten the regional supply outlook.

Headline: India’s Maize Production Forecast at 52.0 Million Tonnes in 2026/27
Summary: According to the USDA August 2026 report, India’s maize production for 2026/27 is forecast at 52.0 million tonnes, unchanged from the July estimate and lower than 55.1 million tonnes in 2025/26. The yield is projected at 3.6 tonnes per hectare, compared with 3.8 tonnes per hectare last year. Total maize supply is estimated at 59.6 million tonnes, supported by beginning stocks of 7.5 million tonnes and imports of 0.1 million tonnes. Domestic consumption is forecast at 52.0 million tonnes, including 30.0 million tonnes for feed and 22.0 million tonnes for FSI use. Meanwhile, exports are projected at 1.5 million tonnes, while ending stocks are expected at 6.1 million tonnes.

Headline: Andhra Pradesh Maize Sowing Down 31.9% YoY at 88.9 Thousand Hectares as of August 12
Summary: According to the Andhra Pradesh Department of Agriculture, maize sowing in the state stood at 88.9 thousand hectares as of August 12, 2026, compared with 130.4 thousand hectares during the corresponding period last year, marking a 31.9% year-on-year decline. The current acreage has covered 57% of the normal seasonal area of 157.2 thousand hectares and 62% of the normal area expected to be covered by this date (142.6 thousand hectares). The data indicates that maize sowing in Andhra Pradesh is significantly behind last year’s pace and the normal seasonal progress.

Headline: Tamil Nadu Maize Sowing Reaches 530.9 Thousand Acres as of August 12
Summary: According to the latest Vanakalam 2026 sowing data as of August 12, 2026, maize has been sown across 530.9 thousand acres in Tamil Nadu, covering 86% of the normal seasonal area of 616.8 thousand acres. The current acreage is lower than the 596.9 thousand acres recorded during the corresponding period last year, representing a decline of around 11.1% year-on-year. However, sowing remains slightly above the 524.7 thousand acres recorded against the normal area target as of the same date. Overall, maize sowing is progressing close to the seasonal normal, although acreage remains below last year’s level.

Headline: Heavy Rainfall Expected in Key Pulse-Growing States, Raising Mixed Crop Implications
Summary: A depression over coastal West Bengal is expected to move northwest across Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand, bringing heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh on 13–14 August. Widespread rainfall is also forecast over East Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha and West Madhya Pradesh, while Maharashtra and Karnataka are expected to receive further rainfall. The rainfall in key pulses growing state should improve soil moisture for Tur, Urad and Moong, but excessive precipitation could raise waterlogging and crop-damage risks in already saturated areas.

Headline: Karnataka Clears Rs 453 Crore Sugar and Ethanol Project
Summary: Karnataka has approved a Rs 453 crore sugar and ethanol project in Vijayapura district as part of 83 industrial projects with a combined investment of around Rs 6,253 crore. Shrishail Mallikarjun Distillery will establish the sugar plant and ethanol facility in Devarahipparagi taluk. The approvals are expected to support industrial investment and employment, particularly outside Bengaluru, while strengthening Karnataka’s sugar and ethanol sector.

Headline: Tanzania Targets Sugar Self-Sufficiency by 2030, Plans Exports from 2026-27
Summary: Tanzania aims to become self-sufficient in sugar by 2030 and start exporting surplus sugar from the 2026-27 season. Domestic sugar production reached 410,979 tonnes by April 2026, against annual demand of around 550,000 tonnes, while installed production capacity is about 800,000 tonnes. The government is expanding mills, promoting modern farming technologies and supporting small-scale farmers. Tanzania also plans to increase production to reduce imports and eventually supply other African markets.

Headline: Onion Prices Likely to Become Biggest Driver of Food Inflation in July
Summary: After months of high tomato prices, onion prices are expected to become the main contributor to food inflation in July. Retail onion prices increased by nearly 20% year-on-year across states during the month, while potato and tomato prices declined. Although tomato prices remained higher in absolute terms, their inflation eased compared to previous months. The rising onion prices are likely to push overall food inflation higher, making onions the biggest disruptor among the TOP (Tomato, Onion and Potato) basket in July.

Headline: Madhya Pradesh Leads India's Tomato Production in 2025/26
Summary: According to the First Advance Estimates for 2025/26, India's tomato production is estimated at 21.32 MMT, with Madhya Pradesh emerging as the largest producer at 3.62 MMT, followed by Andhra Pradesh (2.70 MMT), Karnataka (2.39 MMT), Gujarat (1.66 MMT), and Odisha (1.51 MMT). India remains the world's second-largest tomato producer after China, with tomatoes accounting for approximately 11% of the country's total vegetable production, highlighting their growing importance in India's horticulture sector.

Headline: Global Potato Summit to Highlight India’s 60-Million-Tonne Crop
Summary: India’s potato industry, with annual production of around 60 million tonnes, is set to gain greater focus at the Global Potato Summit 2026 in Gujarat. The summit will discuss seed innovation, processing, cold storage, mechanisation and export opportunities.India’s potato processing sector is expanding, with around 3 million tonnes of potatoes currently used annually for products such as chips, fries and flakes. Rising demand from food service and modern retail is expected to support further growth.

Headline: Chana Arrivals Decline 7.9% as Core Producing States Report Lower Supplies
Summary: Cumulative chana arrivals in India stood at 1,634 thousand tonnes during March–August 8, down 7.9% from 1,775 thousand tonnes last year. Arrivals declined in key producing states, including Madhya Pradesh (-6.5%), Maharashtra (-4.6%) and Rajasthan (-19.9%), while Uttar Pradesh recorded a sharp 95.2% decline. Karnataka was a major exception, with arrivals rising 1,833.3% to 174 thousand tonnes. The overall supply contraction is supporting firm chana prices, with tighter availability in the core production belt likely to remain a key market factor.

Headline: Chana Prices Turn Higher After Mid-Year Reversal
Summary: Chana prices at Delhi averaged ₹61,185 per tonne in July 2026, up 0.66% from ₹60,785 per tonne last year, while August prices averaged ₹63,786 per tonne up to 13 August, 1.63% higher year-on-year. Prices remained above the five-year average, indicating a firm market, while still below historical seasonal highs. Seasonal trends suggest prices could remain elevated through September–October before easing towards year-end.

Headline: Chennai Port; Pulses Imports Reach 32,200 MT During 1–9 August
Summary: Chennai received 32,200 tonnes of pulses in 1,288 containers during 1–9 August 2026. Urad accounted for the largest share, with 21,925 tonnes from Myanmar and Brazil, followed by Masoor at 6,675 tonnes from Russia and Canada. Tur imports stood at 2,700 tonnes, while cow peas, rajma and bocarte beans accounted for the balance.

Headline: Uttar Pradesh Accounts for Nearly 78% of Maize Arrivals During August 3–11
Summary: Maize arrivals across major mandis reached 201.0 thousand tonnes during August 3–11, 2026, with Uttar Pradesh contributing 155.7 thousand tonnes, accounting for nearly 78% of total arrivals. Karnataka followed with 19.6 thousand tonnes, while Madhya Pradesh recorded 9.1 thousand tonnes and Punjab reported 5.4 thousand tonnes. Chhattisgarh was another notable contributor with 3.9 thousand tonnes, while Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana recorded arrivals ranging between 1.0 and 1.8 thousand tonnes. The strong concentration of arrivals in Uttar Pradesh indicates that the state remained the key source of maize market arrivals during the period.

Headline: Maharashtra’s Kharif Maize Sowing Reaches 1,259 Thousand Hectares
Summary: Maharashtra’s kharif maize sowing has surpassed normal levels during the 2026 season, with 1,259 thousand hectares covered as of August 10, 2026, against a normal area of 934 thousand hectares, achieving 135% of the normal level. Ahilyanagar recorded sowing at 163% of normal, while Jalgaon registered the highest coverage at 185%. The Nashik division reached 149% of normal maize acreage, followed by Kolhapur at 141%. However, sowing remained significantly lower in the Latur division, at just 59% of normal.

Headline: Tamil Nadu’s Theni District Offers Subsidised Maize Seeds to Support Cultivation
Summary: The Agriculture Department in Theni district, Tamil Nadu, has announced subsidised maize seed distribution under the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission to support farmers and reduce cultivation costs. Farmers will receive ADVANTA-ADV 752 maize seeds at a subsidy of ₹100 per kg, bringing the effective price to ₹290 per kg, with coverage available for up to 2 acres per farmer. The subsidy is expected to improve access to quality seed and encourage maize cultivation in the district. Higher maize acreage could support additional production and improve local availability in the coming season, while steady demand from poultry, feed and industrial users may provide support to consumption. The overall impact on supply will depend on farmer participation and the resulting increase in production.

Headline: Bihar Moves to Fast-Track Land Disputes to Support Sugar Industry
Summary: Bihar has directed officials to speed up the resolution of land disputes affecting sugar mills, with the aim of preventing delays in mill operations and future expansion. The government is reviewing pending cases involving both government and private land and has asked officials to provide updated ownership records, revenue documents and other evidence to courts. Major disputes involving Bara Chakia, Hanuman Sugar and Industries, and Sasamusa sugar mills are being reviewed. Faster resolution of these cases could support the revival and expansion of Bihar’s sugar industry.

Headline: USDA Maintains 2026–27 U.S. Corn Use for Ethanol at 5.6 Billion Bushels
Summary: The USDA has maintained its forecast for U.S. corn use in fuel ethanol production at 5.6 billion bushels for the 2026–27 marketing year in its August WASDE report. The estimate remains unchanged, indicating steady demand for corn from the ethanol sector. The USDA also raised its 2026–27 U.S. corn production forecast, with higher planted area partly offset by lower expected yields. Stable ethanol demand, alongside changes in overall corn supply, will remain an important factor for the U.S. corn balance sheet. Ethanol continues to account for a significant share of domestic corn consumption, providing underlying support to the corn market even as production and export prospects change.

Headline: Kenya Faces Nearly 486 Thousand-Tonne Maize Deficit by Late September
Summary: Kenya is projected to face a maize deficit of nearly 486 thousand tonnes by the end of September 2026 as adverse weather and delays in input supplies weigh on domestic production. The country’s Agriculture Cabinet Secretary has warned that maize output could decline by up to 40%, with dry conditions following early rainfall affecting crop establishment and flowering in key growing areas, including the North Rift.The supply shortage is expected to keep pressure on maize prices, with sustained demand and higher transport costs adding to market tightness.
